pages.text: Milo the mobile phone buzzes softly in a pocket. He is small, but inside him lives a powerful tiny computer.
When someone taps Milo’s screen, his tiny computer wakes up and follows instructions very fast.
Milo talks to tall phone towers nearby. These towers help phones send signals through the air.
Voices, texts, and pictures turn into digital signals. Signals travel quickly so messages arrive in seconds.
Milo loves taking photos. Light enters the camera and becomes a picture saved inside the phone.
Inside Milo is a battery. The battery stores energy that keeps the phone working all day.
When the battery gets low, Milo needs rest. Plugging into a charger fills the battery again.
Phones are helpful tools. They can show maps, play music, and help families talk from far away.
Too much screen time can tire eyes and minds. Taking breaks helps bodies feel better.
At night, Milo rests on the charger. Tomorrow, he will help again with learning, sharing, and connecting.
